post.description:
Create a payout in one of two ways:
- **Payout without quote** — specify the beneficiary, currencies and amount inline. Fees and the FX
  rate are determined at creation time (`CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest`).

- **Payout with quote** — pass a `quote_id` from `POST /quotes` (with `resource: payout`) to settle
  against a locked rate and fee breakdown. The currencies, amount and payment rail are derived from
  the quote and must not be sent (`CreatePayoutWithQuoteRequest`).

The request variant is selected by the presence of `quote_id`.
If payout queueing is enabled on your account and the balance in the source currency does not cover the amount plus fees, the payout is accepted with `status: queued` instead of being rejected. Glomo releases it automatically once the balance covers it. Fees and the FX rate are fixed at creation and honoured when the payout is released. Without payout queueing, a short balance is rejected at creation.

400.description:
Bad Request — validation error. For quote-based payouts, possible messages include `quote_id not found`, `quote_id has expired`, `quote_id has already been used`, `source_amount cannot be specified when quote_id is present` (likewise for any other quote-derived field), `Quote is not compatible with the selected beneficiary` (the quote's rail is not supported by the chosen beneficiary), and `Quote is not a payout quote` (the `quote_id` belongs to a payin quote).
When the balance does not cover the payout and payout queueing is not enabled on your account, the message reads `Account has insufficient balance to process this transaction. Additional amount required: N.` where `N` is the shortfall, in the smallest unit of the source currency.

409.description: A payout with this `request_id` already exists

message.example: A payout with this request_id already exists

get.description:
Returns a list of your payments, sorted by creation date with the most recent first.

Filters combine with AND, with one exception: `payin_id` and `subscription_id` are mutually exclusive
and sending both returns `400`.

The `status` filter accepts only `in_progress`, `success`, `failed` and `action_required`; any other
value returns `400`. That is not the same set of values a payment can come back with, and the filter
does not map onto the response field one-for-one: a payment returned with `status: under_review` is
matched by `status=in_progress`, and some payments returned with `status: in_progress` are not matched
by `status=in_progress` at all. Treat the filter as a coarse narrowing and read `status` on each
payment you get back.

`compliance_status` is a separate field with its own filter and moves independently of `status`. Most
payments have no compliance status at all, so filtering on it will exclude them.

CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest.title: CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest
CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest.description: Create a payout without a quote by specifying the beneficiary, currencies and amount. Fees and the FX rate are determined at creation time. Use this variant when you have not pre-generated a quote. To create a payout against a locked quote instead, see `CreatePayoutWithQuoteRequest`.

beneficiary_id.description: The unique identifier for the beneficiary.

source_currency.description: The currency from which the amount is deducted from your source balance.

destination_currency.description: The currency in which the beneficiary receives the payout. The currency code is in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format.

source_amount.description:
The amount you intend to send, in the smallest unit of the source currency (e.g. 1000 equates to $10.00 in USD).

Exactly one of `source_amount` or `destination_amount` must be provided (not both).

destination_amount.description:
The amount the beneficiary will receive, in the smallest unit of the destination currency (e.g. cents for USD, paisa for INR).

Exactly one of `source_amount` or `destination_amount` must be provided (not both).

payment_rail.description: The payment rail to use for this payout. Each local rail serves one corridor and is only available when `destination_currency` matches it: `upi`, `imps`, `neft`, `rtgs` for `INR`; `ipp`, `fts` for `AED`; `sepa` for `EUR`; `fps` for `GBP`. `swift` is used for international transfers and is available on any corridor. The rail must be eligible for the beneficiary and the amount must fall inside the rail's limits. Defaults to `swift` if omitted; a local rail is not selected automatically.

invoice_number.description: An optional invoice reference for this payout.

request_id.description: A unique client-generated identifier for this payout request. If a payout with the same `request_id` already exists for your business, the API returns a `409 Conflict` response. Use this to safely retry payout creation without risk of creating duplicates. You can look up the existing payout using `GET /v1/payouts?request_id=<your_request_id>`.

documents.description: List of document IDs to attach to the payout.

CreatePayoutWithQuoteRequest.title: CreatePayoutWithQuoteRequest
CreatePayoutWithQuoteRequest.description: Create a payout against a previously generated quote (see `POST /quotes` with `resource: payout`). The quote locks the fees, FX rate, currencies, amount and payment rail. The locked fields (`source_amount`, `destination_amount`, `source_currency`, `destination_currency`, `payment_rail`) must NOT be sent — including any of them returns a `400 Bad Request`.

quote_id.description: The identifier of a payout quote generated via `POST /quotes`. The quote must exist for your business, must be a payout quote, must not have expired, and must not already have been used for another payout.

beneficiary_id.description: The unique identifier for the beneficiary. The quote's payment rail must be supported by this beneficiary, otherwise the request returns a `400 Bad Request`.

invoice_number.description: An optional invoice reference for this payout.

request_id.description: A unique client-generated identifier for this payout request. If a payout with the same `request_id` already exists for your business, the API returns a `409 Conflict` response. Use this to safely retry payout creation without risk of creating duplicates. You can look up the existing payout using `GET /v1/payouts?request_id=<your_request_id>`.

documents.description: List of document IDs to attach to the payout.

id.description: The unique identifier for the payin.

destination_amount.description:
The amount the beneficiary will receive, expressed in the smallest unit of the specified currency (e.g., cents for USD, paisa for INR). 
      For example, 1000 represents $10.00 in USD. The actual currency is determined by the currency field. Note: "cents" is used generically to denote 
      the minimal currency unit, not necessarily USD.

destination_currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

source_amount.description: The amount you intend to send, also specified in the smallest unit of the selected currency. For example, 1000 equates to $10.00 in USD. The currency field determines which currency is used. As with destination_amount, "cents" is a placeholder for the minimal unit, not specifically USD.

source_currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

beneficiary_id.description: The unique identifier for the beneficiary.

documents.description: The attached documents for the payout.

purpose_code.description: Purpose code for why you want to receive this payment

mid_market_rate.description: The mid-market rate at the time of payout creation. The currency represents the destination currency and rate represents the factor of conversion. Example: 1 EUR = 1.17 USD. Rate corresponds to 1.17 and currency is USD.

currency.description: The currency code for the FX fee

amount.description: The amount of the FX fee

fx_fee.description: The foreign exchange fees applied to the payout

currency.description: The currency code for the transaction fee

amount.description: The amount of the transaction fee

txn_fee.description: The transaction fees applied to the payout

fees.description: The fees applied to this payout

created_at.description: Timestamp representing when the payout was created

updated_at.description: Timestamp representing when the payout was last updated

utr.description: (Optional) Unique Transaction Reference for the payout. This is a unique identifier assigned by the bank to track the transaction.

request_id.description: The client-provided unique identifier for this payout request. Can be used to look up the payout via `GET /v1/payouts?request_id=<your_request_id>`.

payment_rail.description: The payment rail used to settle this payout. Each local rail serves one corridor: `upi`, `imps`, `neft`, `rtgs` for `INR`; `ipp`, `fts` for `AED`; `sepa` for `EUR`; `fps` for `GBP`. `swift` is used for international transfers.

invoice_number.description: The invoice reference provided when the payout was created.

fee_collection_mode.description: How fees for this payout are collected.

error_code.description:
A machine-readable code describing why the payout failed or was cancelled. `null` unless the
payout is in an error state. The accompanying `error_description` carries the human-readable text.

| Code | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `QUOTE_EXPIRED` | Quote has expired. Please create a new payout with a valid quote. |
| `QUEUE_EXPIRED` | Payout stayed queued for 30 days because the balance did not cover it. No funds were held. |
| `PAYOUT_REJECTED` | Payout was rejected by the bank. Please reach out to support. (default fallback) |
| `INVALID_BENE_ACCOUNT_NUMBER` | Beneficiary account number is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_ACCOUNT_TYPE` | Beneficiary account type is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_IFSC` | Beneficiary IFSC code is invalid. |
| `INVALID_VPA` | VPA/UPI address is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_NAME` | Beneficiary name is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_ADDRESS` | Beneficiary address or PIN/ZIP code is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_EMAIL` | Beneficiary email is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_CONTACT` | Beneficiary contact/mobile number is invalid. |
| `NAME_MISMATCH` | Remitter and beneficiary names do not match for the selected purpose. |

error_description.description: A merchant-facing, human-readable description of the error. Operational copy for the merchant. `null` unless the payout is in an error state. See `customer_error_description` for the copy meant for the end-customer.

customer_error_description.description: Customer-facing error copy, written for the merchant to relay to their end-customer. Derives from the same `error_code` as `error_description` but targets a different audience. `null` when there is no `error_code`, or when the error code has no customer-facing variant (some codes are merchant-only).

quote_id.description: The identifier of the quote this payout was created against. `null` for payouts that were not created from a quote.

name.description: The name of the tax withheld.

amount.description: The tax amount, in the smallest unit of `currency`. For example, 877 is 8.77 INR.

currency.description: The currency the tax was withheld in, in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format.

bps.description: The rate the tax was charged at, in basis points. 1800 is 18%.

taxes.description: Taxes withheld on this payout, deducted from the amount before it reached the beneficiary. Present on repatriation payouts (purpose code `P0001`), where the remitting bank withholds GST on the currency conversion; empty for every other purpose, and empty until the bank has confirmed the payout.

id.description: The unique identifier for the payment.

payin_id.description: The unique identifier for the payin. This is set only for payments associated to a payin.

payin_type.description: The type of the payin. This is set only for payments associated to a payin.

subscription_id.description: The unique identifier for the subscription. This is set only for subscription-related payments.

compliance_status.description: The compliance review status of the payment. Present only for payments that have been screened for sanctions or transaction-monitoring holds; `null` for payments that were not screened. This is separate from `status` — a payment can be `status: success` while `compliance_status` is `action_required`, meaning the payment itself completed but funds are held pending compliance review. See the `rfi` field for what's required when `action_required`.

rfi.description: Present only when a compliance-related Request For Information exists on this payment. Describes why the payment was flagged and what's required to resolve it.

id.description: The unique identifier for the RFI.

reason_code_description.description: A human-readable description of why this payment was flagged for compliance review.
reason_code_description.example: The payment has been flagged for a compliance review and requires additional information before it can credited to your account.

reason_code.description: A machine-readable code for the compliance review reason.

response_deadline.description: The deadline by which the requested documents must be submitted. `null` when no deadline has been set.

documents_required.description: Present only when `compliance_status` is `action_required`. The documents needed to resolve this RFI. Submit documents against a specific requirement using its `rfi_doc_id` via the [Respond to an RFI](/api-reference/openapi/rfi/respondrfi) endpoint, passing the `rfi.id` as the RFI identifier.

rfi_doc_id.description: The unique identifier for this document requirement.

description.description: A human-readable description of what document is needed.

multiple_allowed.description: Whether more than one document can be submitted for this requirement.

max_count.description: The maximum number of documents that can be submitted for this requirement.

payment_currency.description: The currency in which the customer pays. The currency code is in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, AED.

payment_amount.description: The total amount the customer pays in cents (includes customer-borne fees if applicable). For example, 374580 cents is 3,745.80 AED. The currency is determined by the `payment_currency` field.

converted_currency.description: The settlement currency after conversion. The currency code is in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

converted_amount.description: The final amount after currency conversion in cents (includes all fees). For example, 102000 cents is $1,020.00. The currency is determined by the `converted_currency` field.

requested_currency.description: The currency that was originally requested by the merchant. The currency code is in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

requested_amount.description: The amount originally requested by the merchant in cents, excluding customer-borne fees. For example, 100000 cents is $1,000.00. The currency is determined by the `requested_currency` field.

purpose_code.description: The purpose code of the payment. This should match the purpose code of the payin.

notes.description: Custom field values for this payment. See [Custom Fields](/payin/custom-fields).

error_description.example: The payment attempt was declined. This could be due to issuer rejection, risk assessment, or restrictions on the card or account. The customer should contact their bank or try a different payment method.

customer_error_description.description: Customer-facing error copy, written for the merchant to relay to their end-customer. Derives from the same `error_code` as `error_description` but targets a different audience. `null` when there is no `error_code`, or when the error code has no customer-facing variant (some codes are merchant-only, e.g. `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`, `LOGGED_IN_ELSEWHERE`, `FUNCTIONALITY_RESTRICTED`).
customer_error_description.example: Your payment could not be completed. Please try a different payment method or contact your bank.

fee_bearer.description: The party bearing the fees for the payment.

fee_collection_mode.description: When merchant-borne fees are collected. `immediate` deducts fees up front; `deferred` invoices them later. `null` when not applicable.

The category of the beneficiary.

- `payout` — the primary use case. Processes a payout from your Glomo balance.

bank_account.description:
The bank account details of the beneficiary.

For `category: payout`, `name` and `address` are resolved from the `swift_code`, the
`local_routing_number`, or an IBAN `account_number`. Send them only if the identifier cannot be
resolved, or to override the resolved values. Both remain required for `category: lrs`.

Routing identifier rules differ by category:

- `category: lrs` — `local_routing_number` is required. `swift_code` is optional.
- `category: payout` — provide exactly one of `swift_code` or `local_routing_number`, except
  for EUR and AED accounts identified by an IBAN alone, which send neither.

For the rails each identifier maps to, see
[Payout rails](/payout/rails).

nickname.description: A nickname for the beneficiary. If not provided, auto-generated as "{beneficiary_name} - {bank_name}".

address_line1.description: The street address of the beneficiary.

address_line2.description: The second line of street address of the beneficiary.

city.description: The city where the beneficiary is located.

state.description: The state or administrative area where the beneficiary is located.

country_code.description: The country where the beneficiary is located. Country should be sent as a [ISO 3166-1 alpha-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3) code.

postal_code.description: The postal code of the beneficiary's address.

bank_account.description: The bank account details of the beneficiary.

account_number.description: The account number of the beneficiary.

name.description: The name of the bank where the account is held.

swift_code.description: The SWIFT/BIC code of the bank. Must be 8-11 characters with first 6 being letters only.

local_routing_number.description: The local routing code or domestic clearing code of the bank account. For reference, this is the IFSC code in India, SORT in UK, ABA in the US, etc.

currency.description: The currency of the bank account.

address_line1.description: The street address of the bank.

address_line2.description: The second line of street address of the bank.

city.description: The city where the bank is located.

state.description: The state or administrative area where the bank is located.

country_code.description: The country where the bank is located. Country should be sent as a [ISO 3166-1 alpha-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3) code.

postal_code.description: The postal code of the bank's address.

intermediate_bank.description: Details of the intermediate/correspondent bank. Present for LRS category beneficiaries (swift_code is required at creation). May be null for payout category beneficiaries.

name.description: The name of the intermediate bank.

country.description: The country of the intermediate bank. Country should be sent as a [ISO 3166-1 alpha-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3) code.

swift_code.description: The SWIFT code of the intermediate bank.

account_number.description: The account number at the intermediate bank.

status.description: The current review status of the beneficiary.

documents.description: List of document IDs attached to the beneficiary.

upi_account.description: The UPI account details of the beneficiary. Present when the beneficiary uses UPI, otherwise null.

upi_id.description: The UPI ID of the beneficiary.

created_at.description: Timestamp representing when the beneficiary was created in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp representing when the beneficiary was last updated in ISO 8601 format.

id.description: The unique identifier for the customer.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phone.description: The phone number of the customer, with country code. Phone number validation is done using the [phonelib](https://github.com/daddyz/phonelib?tab=readme-ov-file) library.

dob.description: The date of birth of the customer

tax_identification_number.description: **Applicable only to the LRS (Liberalised Remittance Scheme / resident-India remittance) flow.** The customer's PAN (tax identification number), populated only for customers onboarded under LRS and absent otherwise. Searchable via the `tax_identification_number` query parameter on the list-customers endpoint.

address.description: The street address of the customer.

city.description: The city where the customer is located.

state.description: The state where the customer is located.

country.description: The country where the customer is located. Country should be sent as a [ISO 3166-1 alpha-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3) code.

pincode.description: The postal code/pincode of the customer's address. [List of countries where pincode is mandatory](/platform/countries#countries-requiring-pincode) are listed here.

created_at.description: Timestamp representing when the customer was created

updated_at.description: Timestamp representing when the customer was last updated

Notes.description: Optional key-value pairs for attaching custom metadata (e.g. invoice references, project codes). Keys must be strings and cannot collide with reserved field names. If your business has custom field rules configured (e.g. enum constraints), values are validated against those rules. Each key appears as a separate column in CSV report exports, with corresponding values populating the rows.

id.description: The unique identifier for the Document.

rfi_doc_id.description: The unique identifier for the RFI Document. This will be `null` if the document is not an RFI Document.

amount.description: A positive integer representing the smallest currency unit.  For example, if the amount is $299.00, then pass 29900 in this field.  In the case of three decimal currencies, such as KWD, BHD and OMR, to represent an amount of 295.991, pass the value as 295990.  And in the case of zero decimal currencies such as JPY, for amount ￥295, pass the value as 295.

currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

amount.description: The fee amount in the smallest currency unit (cents), aggregated across all rules for this fee bearer. For example, 250 cents is $2.50.

currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

collection_mode.description: When the fee is collected. Customer-borne fees are always collected immediately; merchant-borne fees follow the payment's collection mode.

taxes.description: Taxes applied on this fee (for example, GST). Empty when no tax applies to the underlying rules.

amount.description: The tax amount in the smallest currency unit (cents). For example, 1800 cents is $18.00.

currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

name.description: The name of the tax applied on the fee. For example, GST.

bps.description: The tax rate in basis points. For example, 1800 represents 18%.

BeforeParam.name: before
BeforeParam.description: [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) timestamp in UTC to filter resources created before this time. Use this to avoid `Page drift` issue. See [Pagination parameters](/platform/pagination#parameters) for more details.

AfterParam.name: after
AfterParam.description: [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) timestamp in UTC to filter resources created after this time. Use this to avoid `Page drift` issue. See [Pagination parameters](/platform/pagination#parameters) for more details.

PerPageParam.name: per_page
PerPageParam.description: Number of resources per page. Should be between 1 and 100.

PageParam.name: page
PageParam.description: Page number for pagination. Starts from 1. Get the next page number from the `next` field in the response.
